title: Be to + infinitive; be about to + infinitive
summary: Официальные планы, распоряжения и «судьба» с **be to**, а также ближайшее будущее («вот-вот») с **be about to**, включая **I'm not about to...** как отказ.
ru:
## Что уже известно, а что нового
Планы и намерения вы выражали через going to, will и Present continuous. Две конструкции этого юнита — **be to + инфинитив** и **be about to + инфинитив** — тоньше: первая звучит официально и любима новостями и деловой речью, вторая говорит, что событие произойдёт буквально через мгновение.

## Be to: план, приказ, судьба
**Официальная договорённость или план** (новости, деловой стиль). Это не личное намерение, а то, что «намечено» или «решено кем-то»:
> The prime minister **is to visit** Delhi in March. — Премьер-министр посетит Дели в марте (так запланировано).
> The two banks **are to merge** next spring. — Два банка должны объединиться будущей весной.
**Приказ, инструкция, запрет.** Говорящий передаёт чужое распоряжение или правило:
> You **are to report** to the manager at nine. — Вы должны явиться к менеджеру в девять.
> Visitors **are not to feed** the animals. — Посетителям нельзя кормить животных.
**Цель в условии: if ... be to.** Значение «если мы хотим (чтобы)»:
> If we **are to** finish on time, we must start today. — Если мы хотим уложиться в срок, надо начинать сегодня.
**Заголовки.** Глагол be опускается: «PM **to resign**», «Talks **to resume** on Monday».

## Was/were to: «судьба» и несбывшийся план
**was/were to + инфинитив** — в рассказе о прошлом сообщает, что произошло позже (часто то, о чём герой не подозревал):
> She **was to become** the first woman to lead the company. — Ей предстояло стать первой женщиной во главе компании.
**was/were to have + причастие** — план, который не осуществился:
> The talks **were to have started** on Friday (but they didn't). — Переговоры должны были начаться в пятницу (но не начались).

## Be about to: «вот-вот»
**be about to + инфинитив** — действие произойдёт в ближайшие секунды или минуты. Часто с **just**; в прошлом — «собирался, и тут...»:
> Hurry up, the film **is about to** start. — Скорее, фильм вот-вот начнётся.
> I **was just about to** call you when you rang. — Я как раз собирался тебе звонить, когда ты позвонил.
**Отрицание I'm not about to...** означает решительный отказ:
> I'm **not about to** apologise to him. — Я и не думаю перед ним извиняться.
Практический предел: с конкретным временем **about to** не сочетается. ~~He is about to leave on Friday.~~ → He **is to leave** on Friday.

## Сравнение
- **is to** — официально, по плану/распоряжению: The summit **is to take place** in May.
- **is about to** — сию минуту: The summit **is about to** begin.
- **is going to** — нейтрально, намерение/признаки: It's going to rain.
- **is due to** — по расписанию (поезд, рейс), см. следующий юнит.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~The train is about to leave at 6.40.~~ → The train **is to leave** / **is due to leave** at 6.40.
- ~~You are to not touch it.~~ → You **are not to** touch it.
- ~~I was about to have called.~~ → I **was about to call**. (was to have + причастие — другая конструкция.)
- ~~I'm not to apologise~~ в значении «ни за что не стану» → I'm **not about to** apologise. (**I'm not to** значит «мне не велено».)
en:
## What is new here
You already use going to, will and the present continuous for plans. **Be to + infinitive** and **be about to + infinitive** are more specific: the first is formal and typical of news and official language, the second says that something will happen almost at once.

## Be to: plans, orders, destiny
**Official arrangements** (news, business):
> The prime minister **is to visit** Delhi in March.
> The two banks **are to merge** next spring.
**Instructions, orders and rules** that come from someone else:
> You **are to report** to the manager at nine.
> Visitors **are not to feed** the animals.
**Purpose in an if-clause** (= if we want to ...):
> If we **are to** finish on time, we must start today.
**Headlines** leave out the verb be: 'PM **to resign**'.

## Was/were to: destiny and unfulfilled plans
**was/were to + infinitive** tells us what happened later, often without the person knowing it at the time:
> She **was to become** the first woman to lead the company.
**was/were to have + past participle** shows a plan that did not happen:
> The talks **were to have started** on Friday (but they didn't).

## Be about to: very soon
**be about to + infinitive** = at the very moment, almost now. In the past it is often used with **just**, and something interrupts:
> Hurry up, the film **is about to** start.
> I **was just about to** call you when you rang.
**I'm not about to...** expresses firm refusal:
> I'm **not about to** apologise to him.
We do not use about to with a definite future time: ~~He is about to leave on Friday.~~ → He **is to leave** on Friday.

## Comparison
- **is to** — official plan or order.
- **is about to** — immediately.
- **is going to** — neutral intention or evidence.
- **is due to** — according to a timetable.

## Common mistakes
- ~~The train is about to leave at 6.40.~~ → The train **is to leave** at 6.40.
- ~~You are to not touch it.~~ → You **are not to** touch it.
- ~~I was about to have called.~~ → I **was about to call**.
- I'm **not to** apologise = I have been told not to; I'm **not about to** apologise = I refuse.
structure:
## Формулы
| Форма | Построение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| план / приказ | am/is/are (not) **to** + V | The CEO **is to meet** investors on Monday. |
| пассив | am/is/are **to be** + V3 | The results **are to be announced** at noon. |
| «судьба» | was/were **to** + V | He **was to become** a judge. |
| несбывшийся план | was/were **to have** + V3 | The ship **was to have sailed** at six. |
| вот-вот | am/is/are (just) **about to** + V | The train **is about to** leave. |
| «собирался, как вдруг» | was/were (just) **about to** + V | I **was about to** leave when it rang. |
| категорический отказ | am/is/are **not about to** + V | I'm **not about to** pay. |

## Значение: форма, смысл, пример
| Форма | Смысл | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| are **not to** | запрет, инструкция | Staff **are not to** use the lift. |
| are **not about to** | отказ, нежелание | We're **not about to** give up. |
| If we **are to** | цель, «чтобы» | If we **are to** win, we need a plan. |
| **was to** (+ V) | позднее случилось | She **was to** win the prize twice. |
| **was to have** + V3 | не случилось | The prize **was to have been** hers. |

## Отрицание и вопрос
> **Is** the minister **to** speak today? — Нет, **he isn't**.
> The staff **are not to** enter. / **Were** the talks **to** take place in May?
> Be about to: **Is** the plane **about to** land? — Yes, it is.

exercises.title: Be to: какая форма be?
exercises.instruction: Вставьте нужную форму глагола be (is, are, was или were).
exercises.example: The summit ___ to take place in May. → **is**

items.text: The new terminal {{is}} to be opened by the governor in October.
Pupils {{are}} not to leave the school grounds during the lunch break.
The singer {{was}} to become the most successful artist of her generation, but at that time she was still unknown.
The two delegations {{were}} to have met on Friday, but the talks were postponed.
The results {{are}} to be announced at noon tomorrow.
If the project {{is}} to survive, the board must find new funding.

exercises.title: Be about to: вставьте about to

items.text: Quiet, please — the speaker is {{about to}} begin.
I was {{about to}} leave the office when my phone rang.
We were just {{about to}} board when the flight was cancelled.
I'm not {{about to}} apologise to someone who has never once said sorry to me.
The volcano is {{about to}} erupt, scientists have warned.
Ann was just {{about to}} open the door when it swung open from the other side.

exercises.title: Be to или be about to?
exercises.instruction: Выберите форму, которая подходит по смыслу.

items.q: According to the schedule, the CEO ___ investors in Singapore on Monday.
items.why: Официальный план и конкретное время → **is to**. **about to** значит «вот-вот» и с днём недели не сочетается.
Действие произойдёт через секунды → **is about to leave**.

items.q: Guests ___ park in front of the entrance; it is reserved for ambulances.
If we ___ finish before the deadline, we will need two more people.
items.why: If + be to = «если мы хотим (чтобы получилось)».

items.q: The flight ___ have landed at six, but fog delayed it.
items.why: Несбывшийся план в прошлом → **was to have + V3**.

items.q: I ___ apologise to him after the way he spoke to me!
items.why: Категорический отказ в настоящем → **I'm not about to**. **I'm not to** означало бы «мне не велено».

items.q: He ___ leave when the phone rang.
The patients are not to leave the ward.
I wasn't about to give up.
options: Я хотел сдаться, но не успел.
items.why: **not about to** — решительный отказ, нежелание делать что-либо.

items.q: The president was to have addressed the nation.
options: Президент должен был выступить, но не выступил.
items.why: **was to have + V3** — не осуществившийся план.

items.q: The ferry is about to leave.
options: Паром отходит по расписанию в пятницу.
Паром отойдёт с минуты на минуту.

items.q: She was to become a leading physicist.
options: Ей предстояло стать видным физиком (и она стала).
items.why: **was to** в повествовании о прошлом — «суждено было», будущее с точки зрения прошлого.

items.q: If we are to catch the train, we must leave now.
options: Если мы хотим успеть на поезд, надо выходить сейчас.
Если мы вот-вот поймаем поезд, надо выходить сейчас.
Если нам велят ехать на поезде, надо выходить сейчас.
items.why: **If + be to** выражает цель: «чтобы / если мы хотим».

exercises.title: Перепишите с be to / be about to
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя указанную конструкцию. Начало дано.

items.prompt: It has been officially arranged that the Prime Minister will visit Delhi in March. → The Prime Minister ...
answers: The Prime Minister is to visit Delhi in March.
The Prime Minister is to visit Delhi in March

items.prompt: The instructions say you must not open the box before Monday. → You ...
answers: You are not to open the box before Monday.
You aren't to open the box before Monday.
You are not to open the box until Monday.
You aren't to open the box until Monday.

items.prompt: The match will begin in a few seconds. → The match ...
answers: The match is about to begin.
The match is about to start.
The match is just about to begin.
The match is just about to start.

items.prompt: We planned to launch the app in June, but we didn't (was/were to have). → We ...
answers: We were to have launched the app in June.
We were to have launched the app in June, but we didn't.

items.prompt: She is on the point of making a decision. → She ...
answers: She is about to make a decision.
She's about to make a decision.
She is just about to make a decision.
She's just about to make a decision.

items.prompt: In order to succeed, you need to work harder. → If you ...
answers: If you are to succeed, you need to work harder.
If you are to succeed, you must work harder.
If you're to succeed, you need to work harder.
If you're to succeed, you must work harder.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя **be to** или **be about to**.

items.prompt: What is something that is officially planned at your workplace or school (use is/are to)?
items.sample: A new training programme is to start at our company in September.

items.prompt: Describe a moment when you were just about to do something and were interrupted.
items.sample: I was just about to leave for the airport when I realised I had forgotten my passport.

items.prompt: What is something you are not about to do, whatever people say?
items.sample: I'm not about to lend money to someone who never pays it back.

items.prompt: Write about a plan of yours that did not happen (was/were to have + participle).
items.sample: We were to have travelled to Italy last summer, but my husband fell ill.

items.prompt: What are the rules at your place of work or study (are not to ...)?
items.sample: Employees are not to share passwords with colleagues.

items.prompt: Write about a change at your workplace or in your country that is officially planned (is to / are to).
items.sample: The old bus station is to be replaced by a modern terminal next year.
